content.text:
I'd go with what the page picks: open a trading account at Psagot (פסגות ניירות ערך בע"מ) and put 750 ₪ a month into "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)". After 15 years it shows 179,889 ₪, and it says that's "בכסף של היום". I put in 135,000 ₪ in total, so I come out about 45,000 ₪ ahead. Fairly sure. What decided it: it was marked "הבחירה שלכם · ★ הזול" (the cheapest), and I know the name Psagot.

**Inflation:** I tapped the "אינפלציה" button and the window says 2% a year ("בכמה המחירים עולים בשנה, בממוצע"). The 7% a year return was already filled in and I left it.

**How it went:**
- The heading "איפה ואיך הכי זול להשקיע במדד, לאורך זמן" was what I wanted, so I stayed.
- I typed 0 as the starting amount, 750 a month and 15 years. The fields took my numbers fine. The monthly slider shows 800 but the box says 750, so I went with the box.
- The first big number, 179,889 ₪, is the one that stuck. The next pair was only 122 ₪ less, so I didn't bother with it.
- I scrolled once and saw a bar for "כמה זה עולה לכם ב־15 שנים": about 18,300 ₪ in total. Most of it is pink. Going by the legend I think pink is "מס" (tax), around 15,000 ₪. The small yellow and orange parts I'm guessing are the account's fees.
- The fund card shows "דמי ניהול: 0% קבוע, 0% משתנה, 0.02% נאמן", so the fees look like basically nothing. Psagot costs 2,604 ₪ over the 15 years.
- I didn't open "התעריפון" or "כל הקרנות" and didn't read "העמלות זו על זו".

**Words I didn't get:** "דמי משמרת", "נאמן", "(4D)", and the 3.17 ₪ dollar rate, which comes with something about a European central bank (I don't get why that's here). I also don't know what "הזוג" (the pair) means. I took it to be the account plus the fund. "אם הדולר לא זז מול השקל" (if the dollar doesn't move against the shekel) sat under the big number, and I skipped it.

**What bothered me:**
- It cost me about 18,000 ₪ and I hadn't expected that. Most of it is tax, and it took me a while to work that out from the colours.
- I don't know Yalin Lapidot as well as I know the banks.
- I'm not sure whether the 7% already has inflation taken off or not.
